record.paper_title: Resolution of Some Open Problems Concerning Multiple Zeta Evaluations of Arbitrary Depth
record.context_brief: Conjectured generating function for alternating unit Euler sums
record.original_question: Let A(z) = Σ_{n=0}^{∞} z^n ζ({̅1}^n), using the alternating Euler-sum notation of the source. For every complex number t, does the generating function identity Σ_{n=0}^{∞} [t^{2n} ζ({̅1, 1}^n) + t^{2n+1} ζ(̅1, {̅1, 1}^n)] = A(t/(1-i)) A(t/(1+i)) hold?

evidence.quote: COROLLARY 1 (Conjectured in [4]). Let A(z) be as in (12). Then for all complex numbers t, we have Σ [t^{2n} z({1, 1}^n) + t^{2n+1} z(1,{1, 1}^n)] = A(t/(1 - i)) A(t/(1 + i)).
Other results we provide settle three of the remaining outstanding conjectures of Borwein, Bradley, and Broadhurst.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For positive integers $s_1,\dots,s_d$ and signs $\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_d\in\{+1,-1\}$, define the alternating multiple zeta value
$$\zeta(\bar s_1^{\,\varepsilon_1},\dots,\bar s_d^{\,\varepsilon_d}) \;=\; \sum_{k_1>k_2>\cdots>k_d\ge 1}\;\prod_{j=1}^{d}\frac{\varepsilon_j^{\,k_j}}{k_j^{s_j}},$$
where an overline on an argument $s_j$ indicates $\varepsilon_j=-1$ and absence of an overline indicates $\varepsilon_j=+1$. For a finite string $w$ of (possibly barred) positive integers, let $w^n$ denote the concatenation of $n$ copies of $w$, with $w^0$ the empty string and $\zeta(\emptyset):=1$.

Define
$$A(z) \;=\; \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} z^{n}\,\zeta(\{\bar 1\}^{n}),$$
where $\{\bar 1\}^{n}$ denotes the string of $n$ copies of $\bar 1$.

Prove or disprove: for every complex number $t$ (in the domain of convergence, with the identity holding as an identity of formal/analytic power series),
$$\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\Bigl[\,t^{2n}\,\zeta(\{\bar 1,1\}^{n}) \;+\; t^{2n+1}\,\zeta(\bar 1,\{\bar 1,1\}^{n})\Bigr] \;=\; A\!\left(\frac{t}{1-i}\right)\,A\!\left(\frac{t}{1+i}\right),$$
where $i=\sqrt{-1}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The identity was a conjecture of Borwein, Bradley, and Broadhurst on alternating unit Euler sums, and has been established as a corollary in subsequent work on multiple zeta evaluations of arbitrary depth, which resolved it together with related outstanding conjectures.

status_evidence.claim: The generating-function identity is proved as a corollary, resolving a conjecture of Borwein–Bradley–Broadhurst.
